The func_80040410 argument must be computed into a local before the two flag stores, because the target reads gMain_bMenuID above them and a store through the entry pointer may alias that byte. What remains is 11 positions of register allocation in two clusters, both of the same kind: the target reloads a global pointer into a0 where the candidate picks v1, so the pairing of loads to stores differs. Improved from eleven differing positions to three, still at the exact 221 instructions. The eleven were described as two independent clusters of register allocation; they are not independent. The target's first load of D_80184560 serves both the plus 0x6C and the plus 0x60 store and its second load serves plus 0x36; the build's first load serves plus 0x6C alone and the plus 0x60 store moves onto the second load. Both have two loads for three stores, so the question is which statement re-reads the global, not how many times it is read. The first loop keeps the %hi register for the folded count at offset 0 and a separate materialised base for the elements, which is why it needs six callee-saved registers against the second loop's five. The loop bound is re-read every iteration and the index into the row is i + 1 because entry 0 is the count. The prologue is also solved: the 0x38 frame with both object pointers written to 0x10 and 0x14 of the stack before the first branch is what an aggregate local produces, either u8 *o[2] or a two field struct. Plain locals build a 0x30 frame and keep both pointers in callee-saved registers, and spelling D_801845EC[0] at every use builds a 0x30 frame and re-reads the global rather than the stack. What remains is one CSE behaviour worth 54 instructions. The target reloads the object pointer once per occurrence, so the three chained stores of 0x40 take three separate lw from the same stack slot into three registers, and each compound assignment takes two. Every aggregate spelling tried instead emits one load and reuses it, and with the pointer in a register GCC also fuses the two range tests into a single subtract and unsigned compare where the target reloads and branches twice. It also explains the unfilled load delay slots through the whole first half, because the scheduler may not move anything across a volatile access, while the two loops that touch no volatile object are scheduled normally. The three colour bytes are one chained assignment o[0][0xC] = o[0][0xD] = o[0][0xE] = 0x40, which evaluates the three addresses left to right and then stores right to left, exactly the observed order. The sign flip is a compound assignment, *(s16 *)(o[0] + 0x60) *= -1, so the address is evaluated once and the load is lh; written out as x = -x it evaluates the address twice and loads lhu. The range test is two differently signed reads of the same byte, an unsigned compare against 0x41 and a signed test for negative, which is what gives lbu with sltiu followed by lb with bgez.
